reason: The trigger is real and inside the window: Stegra announced the closing of a €1.4B financing round on 24 June 2026 (company release via PR Newswire / Morningstar), led by a Wallenberg Investments consortium (existing investors IMAS and Temasek, new investors Bolero and SEB-Stiftelsen) with Altor becoming the second-largest shareholder and Hy24, Just Climate, Scania, Schaeffler, Kobe Steel and others following; the row's own source (tech.eu, 14 Apr 2026) is the agreement-in-principle, not the close. But the round does not clear the 1440 bar on deal-capable capacity, and the pipeline's own MD threshold (70) would refuse it: this is a rescue financing for a pre-revenue plant. Creditors engaged Houlihan Lokey and the board discussed insolvency risk in October 2025 (reported); the company put the extra need at ~SEK 10B in November 2025 (reported); the Boden project carries a ~€1B overrun on a ~€7.5B budget (reported), first steel has slipped repeatedly and the company said the project timeline is 'under review' after the June close (reported, Eurometal / Mining Metal News). The release states the use of proceeds as completing construction and commissioning the Boden plant and fortifying the equity ratio — every euro is committed to the plant, and a Wallenberg/Altor/pension-fund cap table would not sanction a multi-year Formula E budget before first steel. Honest score ~47/100 (timing 12, capacity 6, brand fit 13, urgency 8, ops fit 8): no real MODE A workstream exists for a spec-chassis series, no US presence, no Swedish round or team, and no motorsport tie found for CEO Henrik Henriksson (ex-Scania CEO; Head of Communications Karin Hallstan; CFO Markus Holm from 1 Mar 2026; no CMO or CCO listed). Not contradicted, not an existing partner, not stale — simply not a brand-investment moment. Re-open at first steel / commissioning with the timeline confirmed, when the Porsche and Scania (Cupra/VW Group) offtakes give a customer's-team angle at Porsche Formula E Team or Cupra Kiro.
